scenario: A museum curator must assign exactly seven paintings—Fresco, Gauguin, Holbein, Ingres, Jawlensky, Klee, and Leger—to exactly three gallery wings: North, South, and West. The North wing will display exactly three paintings; the South wing will display exactly two paintings; the West wing will display exactly two paintings. The following conditions apply: Fresco is displayed in the North wing. Gauguin and Holbein are displayed in the same wing as each other. Ingres and Jawlensky are displayed in different wings from each other. If Klee is displayed in the South wing, then Leger is displayed in the West wing. Exactly one of Ingres and Klee is displayed in the North wing.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could be a complete and accurate assignment of paintings to wings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: North: Fresco, Gauguin, Holbein; South: Ingres, Jawlensky; West: Klee, Leger

choices.label: B
choices.text: North: Fresco, Ingres, Leger; South: Gauguin, Holbein; West: Jawlensky, Klee

choices.label: C
choices.text: North: Fresco, Klee, Leger; South: Gauguin, Ingres; West: Holbein, Jawlensky

choices.label: D
choices.text: North: Fresco, Ingres, Klee; South: Gauguin, Holbein; West: Jawlensky, Leger

choices.label: E
choices.text: North: Fresco, Jawlensky, Leger; South: Gauguin, Holbein; West: Ingres, Klee

explanations.correct: (B) satisfies every rule: Fresco is in North; Gauguin and Holbein are together in South; Ingres (North) and Jawlensky (West) are in different wings; exactly one of Ingres/Klee (Ingres) is in North; group sizes are 3/2/2.
explanations.A: Violates the exactly-one-of rule: neither Ingres nor Klee is in North.
explanations.C: Violates the different-wing rule for Gauguin and Holbein — they must share a wing, but here Gauguin is in South and Holbein is in West.
explanations.D: Violates the exactly-one-of rule: both Ingres and Klee are in North.
explanations.E: Violates the exactly-one-of rule: neither Ingres nor Klee is in North.

questions.questionStem: If Klee is displayed in the North wing, then which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gauguin is displayed in the South wing.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Holbein is displayed in the West wing.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ingres is displayed in the South wing.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Jawlensky is displayed in the North wing.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Leger is displayed in the North wing.

explanations.correct: If Klee is in North, then by the exactly-one-of rule Ingres is not in North. Fresco and Klee fill two North slots; one North slot remains. Gauguin and Holbein must share a wing — since only one North slot remains and they need two adjacent slots in the same wing, they must share South or West. Ingres (not in North) and Jawlensky must be in different wings, so one of them occupies North's remaining slot. Since Ingres is barred from North, Jawlensky must be in North.
explanations.A: Gauguin could be in South or West.
explanations.B: Holbein could be in South or West.
explanations.C: Ingres could be in South or West — only barred from North.
explanations.E: Leger could be in South or West; with Klee in North, the conditional about Klee being in South is not triggered.

questions.questionStem: If Gauguin is displayed in the West wing, then which one of the following could be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ingres is displayed in the West wing.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Klee is displayed in the South wing.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Leger is displayed in the South wing.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Jawlensky is displayed in the West wing.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Holbein is displayed in the North wing.

explanations.correct: With Gauguin and Holbein both in West, West is full. Fresco is in North. Exactly one of Ingres/Klee is in North; Ingres and Jawlensky are in different wings. One valid assignment: North = Fresco, Ingres, Jawlensky; wait — that violates Ingres/Jawlensky different. Try North = Fresco, Klee, Jawlensky; South = Ingres, Leger; West = Gauguin, Holbein. This satisfies all rules and places Leger in South.
explanations.A: West is full with Gauguin and Holbein; Ingres cannot be in West.
explanations.B: If Klee is in South, then Leger must be in West — but West is full.
explanations.D: West is already full with Gauguin and Holbein.
explanations.E: Holbein must be in the same wing as Gauguin, which is West.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following CANNOT be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gauguin and Holbein are both displayed in the South wing.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ingres and Leger are both displayed in the North wing.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Klee and Jawlensky are both displayed in the North wing.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Klee and Leger are both displayed in the South wing.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Jawlensky and Leger are both displayed in the West wing.

explanations.correct: If Klee is in South, the conditional forces Leger into West. So Klee and Leger cannot both be in South.
explanations.A: Possible — e.g., solution 1 has Gauguin and Holbein both in South.
explanations.B: Possible — Fresco, Ingres, Leger in North (solution 1).
explanations.C: Possible — Klee and Jawlensky both in North alongside Fresco when Ingres is elsewhere.
explanations.D: Correct — violates the conditional rule about Klee in South.
explanations.E: Possible — Jawlensky and Leger can both occupy West when Ingres is in North.

questions.questionStem: If Ingres is displayed in the West wing, then which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Klee is displayed in the North wing.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Jawlensky is displayed in the South wing.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Leger is displayed in the West wing.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gauguin is displayed in the North wing.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Holbein is displayed in the South wing.

explanations.correct: Exactly one of Ingres and Klee is in North. Since Ingres is in West, Klee must be in North.
explanations.B: Jawlensky must differ from Ingres, so Jawlensky is in North or South — not forced to South.
explanations.C: Leger's wing is not forced; Leger could be in North or South.
explanations.D: Gauguin and Holbein share a wing, but that wing need not be North.
explanations.E: Holbein's wing depends on Gauguin; not forced to South.
